guitar.guitaristsText: Gary Rossington (lead) / Allen Collins (rhythm) / Ed King (bass)
guitar.modelsText: Gibson SG Standard (Rossington) / Gibson Firebird I 1964 Reverse (Collins) / Fender bass (King on album, but guitar capable)
guitar.notes: Rossington used cherry-finish 1969 Gibson SG Standard for slide work on 'Free Bird' and other tracks per UDiscover/Gear Guide; sources also cite Gibson Les Paul Standard as his main throughout career. For Gimme Three Steps specifically, lead duties were Rossington's. Allen Collins' 1964 Gibson Firebird I (Reverse, heavily modified) is documented for this session. Ed King played bass on debut album per Wikipedia, so guitar lineup is Rossington + Collins for this track.

tone.target: bright southern rock crunch with upper-mid bite and natural breakup
tone.profile: bright, crunchy rhythm tone emulating classic Marshall Plexi tone with controlled sustain
tone.summary: A bright, driven yet controlled rhythm tone with upper-mid emphasis and minimal effects. Rossington's lead uses natural amp breakup and dynamic playing; Collins' rhythm provides steady crunch with Fender reverb coloration.
gearClues: Fender Super Reverb or Twin (Collins documented)
minimal pedal board (phaser or wah only, rare)
Coricidin bottle slide for Rossington's tone
corrections: Confirmed Marshall 1959T for Rossington in 1973 debut sessions, not Marshall 50W modern head
Collins used Fender amps with Marshall backing; Fender Super Reverb or Twin documented
No evidence of distortion or overdrive pedals in 1973 debut era—minimize effects
Slide work (Coricidin bottle) crucial to Rossington's character on this track

rig.name: Lynyrd Skynyrd - Gimme Three Steps (1973) - Valeton GP-180 Emulation
rig.recommendedGuitar: Gibson SG Standard or Gibson Les Paul Standard (humbucker-equipped) for Rossington lead tone; Gibson Firebird for Collins rhythm (both with medium-heavy gauge strings)

blocks.purpose: Minimal gate to control sustain noise and hum from tube amp emulation.
blocks.gap: 1973 recording had live session noise; gate setting is conservative to preserve dynamics.

blocks.purpose: Bypass—favor natural amp breakup over pedal-based gain.
blocks.gap: 1973 Skynyrd tone relied on tube amp saturation, not pedal coloration.

blocks.purpose: Bypass—Wah not documented for Gimme Three Steps.
blocks.gap: Vox Wah used on other tracks (Call Me the Breeze per Equipboard) but not this one.
Rossington and Collins used tube amp saturation exclusively in 1973.

blocks.purpose: Emulate Marshall 1959T Super Tremolo (Rossington documented for 1973 debut). UK 50 provides classic Plexi tone with natural breakup.
blocks.gap: Exact Marshall 1959T model not available in GP-180; UK 50 is closest Plexi-type emulation. Allen Collins used Fender Super Reverb or Twin (not covered by this single amp model).

alternatives.reason: Slightly lower headroom, but both work for Plexi tone.

blocks.purpose: Marshall 4x12 cabinet characteristic—standard for Rossington's era.
blocks.gap: None—4x12 Marshall is documented for Rossington's rig from 1973 forward.

blocks.purpose: Brighten upper-mids and treble for bite; reduce bass mud for tight rhythm definition.
blocks.gap: 1973 studio recording likely had console EQ; this emulates post-tape character.

blocks.purpose: Bypass—no chorus, tremolo, or phase documented for Gimme Three Steps.
blocks.gap: Rossington used tremolo and phase later (Line 6 MM4 in later years), but 1973 debut was dry.
Studio recording did not feature echo or slapback delay on this track.

blocks.purpose: Add natural room ambience to match 1973 studio session recording.
blocks.gap: Allen Collins' Fender amps had built-in reverb tank; Rossington's Marshall would have had tape echo in studio. Room verb is compromise.

alternatives.reason: Could emulate Collins' Fender reverb character.

blocks.purpose: Output gain control for FRFR or headphone monitoring.

improvements.summary: This rig emulation is close but limited by single-amp constraint. For full authenticity, run dual chains (Marshall for Rossington lead, Fender Super Reverb for Collins rhythm) or accept Marshall-only compromise. Cabinet IR is solid; reverb character could be refined with Spring or Plate to match Fender tone.

proposals.target: Rossington lead (Marshall) + Collins rhythm (Fender Super Reverb)
proposals.recommendedAsset: Two GP-180 chains or hybrid rig with Valeton routing to parallel Marshall/Fender models
proposals.reason: 1973 session used both amps; single UK 50 is compromise.
proposals.whenToUse: When replicating full band tone or isolating Collins' rhythm character
proposals.expectedGain: Authentic dual-guitar shimmer and tonal separation

proposals.recommendedAsset: Spring reverb (to emulate Fender Super Reverb built-in tank)
proposals.reason: Collins' Fender reverb tank contributed to the song's slight wash; Room is generic.
proposals.whenToUse: After amp/cab tuning is locked in

proposals.recommendedAsset: Marshall 1959T 4x12 IR (if available in GP-180 IR library or third-party)
proposals.reason: Enhance vintage Marshall Plexi tone color.

validation.notesForUpdate: Confidence upgraded from 'medium' to 'medium/high' based on primary source corroboration (Equipboard, UDiscover Gear Guide, Premier Guitar Rig Rundown, Wikipedia album liner notes). Key gaps: (1) Single GP-180 amp cannot fully emulate dual Marshall + Fender setup. (2) Reverb character is simplified. (3) No pedal documentation for Gimme Three Steps specifically—applied conservative 'bypass all effects' approach based on era documentation.
